📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #8. Posted per window-expiry (last notified 2026-07-11T11:20:00Z, ~45h ago, past the 24h suppression window).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Re-query p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over the monitor's own window plus a wider surrounding window — expect values in the 0.001-0.2s range. Confirm 0 error logs on service:notifications. This KB explicitly says: if a future occurrence ever shows a genuine elevated p95, treat as a break from the noise pattern and escalate immediately rather than assuming noise.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on file yet

⚠️ Note: this occurrence DID reproduce an elevated value (see below) — breaks from the "cleanest non-reproduction pattern" this entry documented for its first 7 occurrences. Flagging per the KB's own playbook step 4.

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327 ("[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high", fired 2026-07-13T08:43:07Z — synthetic degraded-cycle DD-scan candidate, no Slack MCP read path this session)

Root-cause analysis:
  • DD metric p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over 2026-07-13T08:13:07Z-08:53:07Z (240 datapoints): baseline ~0.0005-0.02s throughout, EXCEPT one outlier of 1578.86s at 08:30:00Z — far larger than any prior documented occurrence (previous max was 34.73s on a sibling low-traffic monitor family). service:notifications status:error env:prod returned 0 hits for the same window.
  • Same single-request-dominates-percentile mechanism as prior occurrences, but the magnitude here suggests a genuinely hung request or a trace-instrumentation artifact, not ordinary statistical noise. Recommend a trace-level look rather than dismissing as routine.

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
  • DD metric (1578.86s outlier): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Anotifications&exp_agg=p95&start=1783930387&end=1783932787
  • DD logs (0 errors): service:notifications status:error env:prod
  • Kibana: n/a — not the evidence datasource for this KB (evidence_source: datadog_apm)

Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (ownership.md Project match: method-nativemobile-ui / method-platform-ui — supersedes a prior note's Component-table "Service Delivery")

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence #574 (chronic pattern, first_seen 2026-05-20).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: Confirm chronic baseline (ES Ocelot warning volume vs 24h-ago) → aggregate timeouts by RequestPath (upstream microservices.methodlocal.int) → check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first (DNS bursts present as Ocelot timeouts) → identify slow downstream via ms-gateway-api Ocelot config → fix options: raise per-route timeout (cheap/masks), scale microservices IIS pool (medium), or profile upstream service under load (root-cause, expensive).
Open Jira: n/a (none filed)

Source alerts: n/a — degraded cycle, no Slack MCP read access this session. Source: DD monitor 77419271, synthetic fire time 2026-07-13T15:08:12Z (state: Alert at scan time).

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/77419271
  • DD logs (XHR errors, method-ui): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-ui%20-%2AResizeObserver%2A%20-%2Asegment%2A%20-%2Asignalr%2A%20-%2Amixpanel%2A%20-%2Ahotjar%2A%20status%3Aerror%20%2Axhr%2A&from_ts=1783954392000&to_ts=1783955292000&live=false — 100 hits, diffuse account fan-out (top coastalready 10%), canonical chronic shape
  • Kibana: https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-07-13T14:53:12Z',to:'2026-07-13T15:08:12Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'Exception.keyword:*TimedOut* OR message:*Ocelot* OR message:*ResponderMiddleware*'))
  • This-window concentration: gateway 178 (356 hits total, 2026-07-13T14:53:12Z–15:08:12Z)

Note: posts because the 24h suppression window elapsed (last posted 2026-07-12T14:08:12Z, ~25h ago) — routine resurfacing, not a new incident. fix_status remains chronic-residual-post-rollback-2026-06-05, unaddressed.

⚠️ Flagging for Ben, outside the mechanical gate: this is the *4th consecutive* occurrence (2026-07-12T14:08Z, 21:48Z, 22:50Z, and this one) where the ES Ocelot/ResponderMiddleware signature confirms cleanly (356 hits this time) but `service:ms-gateway-api status:error` DD Logs returns 0. The prior occurrence's investigation already crossed the "escalate on 3rd consecutive split" threshold it set for itself and recommended a manual look; that recommendation didn't reach a post last cycle because the mechanical suppression gate still applied. Worth a quick check on whether DD Logs' `status:error` facet is simply not capturing Ocelot ResponderMiddleware timeout warnings for ms-gateway-api (a labeling gap — in which case no action needed beyond documenting it), or whether the failure mode has genuinely stopped producing server-side errors (which would mean the original root-cause diagnosis needs re-verification). Full detail: docs/investigations/2026-07-13-b403ea5da5297a3c.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #234 (chronic pattern, first_seen 2026-05-23) — 24h suppression window expired (last posted 2026-07-12T14:41:18Z, ~27h24m ago).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`) — resolved this cycle via ownership.md (runtime-core-api → Vertical App Experience); corrects this KB entry's prior unmapped state.
Playbook: 1) Confirm pattern: run `dd_search.py metric --query 'p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}'` over the fire window — multiple points > 3s confirms the pattern. 2) Confirm latency-only via `dd_search.py logs --query 'service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod'` — expect 0 hits. 3) If ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout co-fires in the same 60-min window with ≥2 alerts each, treat as shared-upstream signal (see that entry's precedence_note) rather than endpoint-specific.
Open Jira: n/a (fix_status: investigating, no Jira filed yet)

Source alerts (1 total, degraded cycle — no Slack MCP read path, synthetic from DD monitor scan):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700 (fired 2026-07-13T18:05:20Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700 — "RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency" (OK at scan time, self-recovered)
  • DD APM traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20%40duration%3A%3E3s&start=1783964120000&end=1783965920000 — 7 of 180 sampled p95 points exceeded the 3.0s threshold (17:35:20-18:05:20Z window), peak 9.47s at 18:02:50Z (ratio 2.16). Dual-endpoint co-spike confirmed: RTC Action Execution p95 also breached 7 points in the same window, peak 7.28s at the same 18:02:50Z timestamp — canonical shared-upstream signature.
  • DD logs: 0 hits for `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` in window — confirms latency-only, no error signal
  • No Redis-error corroboration this occurrence (monitor 227940275 OK, 0 log hits) — unlike several prior occurrences that showed concurrent Redis command errors/timeouts
  • Kibana: n/a — not the evidence datasource for this KB (evidence_source: datadog_apm, latency-only by design)

Note: DD monitor 77419271 (ki-21, gateway XHR errors) fired 6 min earlier (17:59:11Z) this same cycle — the shared-upstream co-fire precedence note requires ≥2 alerts each in the same 60-min window to treat as a joint incident; that threshold isn't met (1 alert each), so processed independently, but flagging the temporal proximity.
